reply.text:
Shoulders respond to a few things: heavy pressing overhead or on an incline, direct lateral raise work for the side delts (most people under-train these), and some rear delt work like face pulls or reverse flyes so the back of the shoulder keeps up. Your chest and back training already hits the front and rear delts a fair amount, so the side delts usually need the most direct attention.

Most lifters do well with 2 to 3 shoulder sessions' worth of work a week, around 10 to 20 hard sets total, spread out rather than crammed into one day. Lateral raises work well in higher reps, 12 to 20, stopped a rep or two shy of failure. Add weight or a rep over time, and keep the form strict, with no swinging.

If you'd like, I can build you a program with a shoulder focus, or a single shoulder session for today. Just tell me which.
